To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gamification can overcome the limitations of PT approaches in the context of sustainable consumption by (1) providing the user with a broader design space, (2) giving the user more autonomy to set goals, and (3) enabling the designer to recognize the relevance different motivational aspects of the social interaction.

the use of gamification elements can support sustainable consumption by providing the user with the opportunity to select goals that are meaningful in his or her context, to relate individual action to social interactions, and to recognize the motivational aspects of social interactions.
gamification is able to support sustainable consumption in a way that persuasive technologies cannot.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how gamification may help to overcome the limitations in the design of persuasive systems for sustainable consumption.

the question of how to design persuasive technologies that are not based on the assumption of a “one size fits all” model for sustainable consumption but rather support the individual user in developing a more sustainable lifestyle.
the design of ICT applications that support behavior change toward sustainable consumption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

gamification is not the silver bullet for sustainable consumption, but that gamification can be an important part of the toolbox for designers who want to develop ICT applications for sustainable consumption.
the potential of gamified applications is high and that they can be used as a valuable tool to support the transition to sustainable consumption.
gamification has great potential in the field of sustainable consumption, and that the use of game elements may overcome the limitations of PT applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not arguing for the use of gamification per se.
gamification is a promising approach for designing sustainable consumption behavior.
gamification is a promising approach to support sustainable consumption, but the current research and practice in this area still needs to overcome several limitations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of gamified systems for sustainable consumption needs to take into account that the user is an actor with agency and autonomy, and that the system should not be designed as a one-way communication channel, but as an environment in which the user can interact with others and with the system.
gamification is a promising approach to motivate users to change their behavior.
a gamification-based design of sustainable consumption applications should be able to support the user’s autonomy and to provide a broader context for the user’s actions.
